Consult Summary:
- Male patient with known heart failure reports 2 weeks of progressive dyspnea worse over the past few days with new bilateral ankle swelling and mild dry cough; no chest pain, palpitations, or fever; clinician notes chest exam and vitals “OK”; plan includes increasing furosemide, ordering labs and echocardiogram, safety-netting, and 1-week follow-up.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Worsening shortness of breath.
- Timeline:
  - Gradual onset over the last couple of weeks.
  - Marked worsening in the last few days.
  - Now breathless with minimal exertion (around the house, walking to shops); needs to sit to catch breath.
  - Bilateral ankle swelling noticed over the past few days; similar to prior heart failure episode.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Mild dry cough (not troublesome).
  - Feels a bit run-down.
  - Denies chest pain.
  - Denies palpitations.
  - Denies fevers/temperature.
  - Appetite/hydration: Eating and drinking normally.
  - Urination: Urinates frequently, attributed by patient to diuretic use.
- Pertinent negatives: No chest pain, no palpitations, no fever.

Past Medical History:
- Heart failure (history of prior episode improved with medication; current symptoms suggest flare-up).
- History suggestive of myocardial infarction approximately 5 years ago:
  - Patient recalls being told it was “more than angina.”
  - Hospitalized for a few days; recovered; no ongoing chest pain reported since.
- Medications:
  - Furosemide — previously 1 tablet daily; dose (mg) and route not documented.
  - Aspirin — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Bisoprolol — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.

Social History:
- Lives alone with two cats (Polly and Tim).
- Employment: Part-time lorry driver; works day shifts only; finds work exhausting; concerned about ability to work if health worsens.
- Tobacco: Former smoker; ~1 pack/day for ~25 years; quit (date not documented).
- Alcohol: Does not drink.
- Exercise: Walks to the shops daily when able.

Family History:
- Father: Died of heart attack in early 60s.
- Mother: Osteoporosis; living.

Physical Examination:
- Clinician statement: Chest examination “OK”; oxygen saturations and blood pressure “OK.” No numeric values provided and no additional exam details documented.

Investigations:
- Planned:
  - Blood tests: Full blood count (to assess for anemia) and kidney function.
  - Echocardiogram to assess cardiac function (anticipated scheduling in 1–2 weeks).
- None reported as completed during this encounter.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Suspected acute exacerbation (flare-up) of chronic heart failure
  - Assessment: Progressive dyspnea over 2 weeks, worse in last few days; new bilateral ankle edema; mild dry cough; no chest pain or fever. Clinician notes normal chest exam and vitals.
  - Plan:
    - Increase Furosemide from 1 tablet daily to 1 tablet twice daily for the next few days (exact tablet strength not documented).
    - Order blood tests: FBC and renal function.
    - Arrange echocardiogram.
    - Follow-up in approximately 1 week to reassess symptoms and results.
    - Safety net: Seek earlier review if symptoms worsen or if chest pain, palpitations, or dizziness occur.

- Issue 2: History of prior myocardial infarction (patient-reported)
  - Assessment: Event ~5 years ago, “more than angina,” brief hospitalization; no current chest pain.
  - Plan:
    - No specific new actions documented today; background risk considered in heart failure management.

- General plan items:
  - Continue current medications as previously prescribed unless otherwise directed (no explicit changes other than furosemide adjustment).
  - Patient understood plan; no additional questions.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements:
  - Exact medication doses, routes, and frequencies (except furosemide frequency) not documented.
  - No vital sign values recorded (BP, HR, SpO2, RR, Temp).
  - No weight, recent weight changes, orthopnea/PND assessment, or baseline functional class documented.
  - No recent lab results or prior echocardiogram findings (ejection fraction) documented.
  - Smoking quit date not documented.
- Internal conflicts: None noted; brief confusion between metoprolol vs bisoprolol resolved (patient confirms bisoprolol).
- Transcript quality: Minor audio/connection issues and occasional incomplete phrases; overall adequate to extract key clinical details.
